attributes.body_ja:
「に限（かぎ）らず」は「(A) だけでなく (B)」を表（あらわ）す文型（ぶんけい）です。これは「に」と五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「限（かぎ）る」、そして文語（ぶんご）助動詞（じょどうし）「ず」の組（く）み合（あ）わせです。「ず」は「ない」と同（おな）じ意味（いみ）を持（も）ち、同（おな）じように動詞（どうし）に付（つ）いて使（つか）われます。

この表現（ひょうげん）は名詞（めいし）の後（あと）に置（お）かれ、文（ぶん）の (B) の部分（ぶぶん）で (A) と同（おな）じ範囲（はんい）やカテゴリーに含（ふく）まれることの説明（せつめい）が続（つづ）きます。

また、(B) の部分（ぶぶん）に「も」を付（つ）けて強調（きょうちょう）することがあります。特（とく）に (B) だけでなく、いくつかほかのものも含（ふく）める場合（ばあい）に「(B) も (C) も」という形（かたち）で使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
に限（かぎ）らず is a sentence pattern in Japanese used that highlights when something is 'not just (A), but (B) too', or 'not only (A), but also (B)'. It is a combination of に, the う-Verb 限（かぎ）る 'to limit', and the literary auxiliary verb ず, which connects with verbs in the same way, and carries the same meaning as ない.

This structure will appear after nouns, before the (B) part of the sentence will go on to explain things that can be included in the same scope or category as (A).

Occasionally, も may be added for extra emphasis in the (B) part of に限らず sentences. This is especially true when several extra things are being indicated, not just (B). For example, '(B) も (C) も'.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: Both に限らず and はもとより express inclusion beyond an initial example but differ in nuance. に限らず highlights that the mentioned case is not the only one, implying a broader range or scope (not only…but also). はもとより, on the other hand, emphasizes that the stated example is obvious or expected, and contrasts it with less obvious or more significant cases, carrying a nuance closer to 'needless to say…even more so'.

attributes.body: Both mean not only…but also, but differ in register and nuance. に限らず stresses inclusiveness, as in 日本に限らず世界中で使われている (Used not only in Japan but worldwide). のみならず is more formal and often adds additional, sometimes surprising, information, as in 彼は日本語のみならず英語も話せる (He speaks not only Japanese but also English).

attributes.body: はもちろん emphasizes something obvious before adding another case, e.g. 日本人はもちろん留学生も来た ('Not only Japanese people but also exchange students came'). に限らず expands the scope of a statement, implying 'not limited to (A), also (B)', e.g. 子供に限らず大人も楽しめる ('Not only children, but also adults can enjoy it').

first_relatable.title: はもちろん
first_relatable.meaning: Not only but also, Let alone, Not to mention, Of course

second_relatable.title: に限らず
second_relatable.meaning: Not just, Not only… but also

attributes.body: Both are fairly formal patterns which convey that something applies to more than one item, but they differ in nuance. ばかりでなく is a relatively straightforward 'Not only (A), but also (B)', e.g. 日本語ばかりでなく、韓国語も話せる 'He can speak not only Japanese, but also Korean.' In contrast, に限らず has a more specific nuance of 'Not limited to (A)', e.g. 学生に限らず誰でも入場できます 'Not limited to students, anyone can enter.'

first_relatable.meaning: Not only…but also, As well as

second_relatable.title: に限らず

attributes.body: をはじめ highlights one example among similar ones, e.g. 日本をはじめ多くの国で使われている ('It's used in many countries, starting with Japan'). に限らず expands the scope beyond the first item, e.g. 学生に限らず誰でも参加できる ('Not limited to students, anyone can participate').

second_relatable.title: に限らず
second_relatable.meaning: Not just, Not only… but also

attributes.body: だけでなく and に限らず both express non-exclusivity, but differ in nuance and formality. だけでなく is a straightforward expression meaning 'not only (A), but also (B)', and is often used in everyday conversation (especially in the variant form だけじゃなくて). In contrast, に限らず has a more formal and academic tone, and carries a slightly different nuance, suggesting that whatever follows is 'not limited to' the thing in question.
